claude.sample_unit: stochastic simulation replications per scenario coordinate

links.outcome: Volatility and performance across adoption sequences (interoperability-first vs automation-first) in simulated oncology pathway
links.effect: Interoperability-led sequenced adoption reduced midtransition volatility versus automation-first; uncoordinated S II to S IV transition had highest SDs of RTTI and throughput (simulation only, stylized parameters).
links.quote: This sequencing effectively reduced midtransition volatility, allowing the system to absorb the governance load of incremental AI automation while maintaining high throughput efficiency throughout the implementation life cycle ( Figure 5B ).

links.outcome: Governance/administrative burden and throughput when AI automation lacks interoperability (simulated)
links.effect: Automation islands (high A, low I) raised RTTI 26% to 37.1 days and cut throughput to 647 patients/year as governance became the bottleneck.
links.quote: In the automation islands scenario ( S II ), we observed the worst system performance, with mean RTTI increasing to 37.1 days, a 26% increase compared to the analog baseline, whereas throughput decreased to 647 patients per year.

links.outcome: False positives and low-yield investigations from highly sensitive AI triage (simulated)
links.effect: High-sensitivity AI triage increased false positive rate, loading diagnostic resources with low-yield investigations that displaced confirmed cancer cases (no numbers given in main text).
links.quote: As shown in Figure S1C in Multimedia Appendix 3 , the high sensitivity of AI triage tools increased the false positive rate.

Whole-system capacity planning for downstream bottlenecks after upstream AI adoption

links.effect: Data-interoperability-led scaling reduced transition volatility vs automation-first; full integration reached 1244 (SD 21.4) patients/year and RTTI 14.9 (SD 0.3) days.
links.quote: Pathway optimization analysis indicated that a coordinated strategy prioritizing early improvements in data interoperability reduced transition volatility compared to an automation-first approach.

links.effect: Automation without data infrastructure increased RTTI by 26% to 37.1 (SD 1.3) days and reduced throughput to 647 (SD 10.1) patients/year due to governance saturation.
links.quote: Isolated automation without data infrastructure led to reduced system performance, increasing RTTI by 26% (37.1, SD 1.3 days) and reducing throughput to 647 (SD 10.1) patients per year due to administrative governance saturation.

links.effect: Full integration improved RTTI to 14.9 days and throughput to 1244/year, but primary bottleneck shifted to chemotherapy infusion units.
links.quote: Therefore, successful upstream AI adoption transferred capacity pressure from diagnostic infrastructure to labor-intensive treatment resources.

links.effect: High-sensitivity AI triage increased false positives; low-yield investigations displaced confirmed cancer cases and competed for biopsy and histology capacity; no numeric rate reported.
links.quote: This influx placed a disproportionate load on diagnostic resources, resulting in low-yield investigations that displaced confirmed cancer cases and competed for biopsy and histology capacity.

links.effect: Automation islands had worse performance: RTTI 37.1 days (+26% vs 29.4 baseline) and throughput 647/year vs 1022/year.
links.quote: While the trajectory toward S IV showed a combined increase in efficiency (lower RTTI) and number of treated patients, S II resulted in higher RTTI and reduced throughput, suggesting that AI automation intensity may become counterproductive when isolated from data interoperability.

unlisted_practices: Using scenario planning coupled with discrete-event simulation to stress-test AI adoption strategies before implementation

links.outcome: downstream capacity bottlenecks and administrative governance saturation
links.effect: Upstream AI shifted binding constraints to downstream chemotherapy units; isolated automation increased RTTI by 26% to 37.1 days and reduced throughput to 647 patients/year due to governance saturation.
links.quote: The model illustrated a structural bottleneck migration: successful upstream AI adoption shifted binding constraints from diagnostic scanners to downstream chemotherapy infusion units, whereas missing data interoperability resulted in governance constraints.

unlisted_practices: Sequencing data interoperability infrastructure before scaling AI automation
